Chapter 17INPUT

The Beyond

Past the mountains the signal ends. People go anyway.

Past the mountains the city's signal ends, and that is where The Beyond begins: the forests, the rivers, the highways, and the temporary towns of speakers, lights and tents that appear in the wilderness for a weekend and vanish. Vancouver people leave the grid for The Beyond and come back different, with rhythms the city has never played and ways of being together the streets did not have before. The Probes bring the machine version of outside news through the port. The Beyond brings the human version, on dusty cars, at dawn. Leave with the old map. Return with something the map cannot name.

The musician comes home from an unnamed temporary gathering beyond the city with a van full of tired friends. The chapter looks back to the previous afternoon: a mountain road, a small camp, a rhythm passed between hands around an ordinary table. Everyone had played the same phrase differently. On the return journey she tries to recover it from a phone recording. There is fabric noise, a van door and someone laughing at the wrong moment. At a roadside stop the friend with the mug taps a version; another friend answers across the bonnet. The musician stops insisting on the missing original. Back in Vancouver, they try the changed rhythm once more before unloading. What returns is something they can share, not something perfectly preserved.

The ruleLeave with the old map. Return with something the map cannot name.

Terminal City · Storybook v0.10.0 · built 2026-09-13
Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented.
Made by Steve Hiehn, a software developer and electronic musician based in Vancouver, Canada. All music was created using a custom DAW, Signals & Sorcery.
